prompt: Caring for children is an important thing of the society. It is suggested that all mothers and fathers should be required to take childcare training courses. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Since childcare is an essential aspect of society, it is suggested that all parents should be required to enrol in courses that teach them how to care for children. I strongly disagree with this view because individuals can acquire parenting skills from their own caregivers and through personal experience, as well as from various available resources.

First and foremost, people can learn useful parenting skills from their own parents. Since they were raised by them, they may have gained practical knowledge that is more applicable than the general and theoretical information provided in formal courses. Moreover, individuals with younger siblings may have already developed useful skills by caring for them, allowing them to apply this experience when raising their own children. For instance, in Saudi Arabia, older daughters in larger families often help their mothers by taking care of their younger siblings.

Furthermore, there are plenty of resources available nowadays that provide information about raising children. Parents can gain knowledge through online blogs, studies, videos, books, and many other free and accessible sources. They can also return to these resources whenever they need specific information. In contrast, formal courses may be less practical, as people can forget much of what they learn once the course ends, while some of the material may not be applicable to real-life situations. For example, many mothers and doctors use TikTok to share advice on childcare, allowing parents to access useful information whenever they need it.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that parents can develop the necessary skills through their caregivers, personal experience, and widely available resources. Therefore, formal courses should not be compulsory.
